To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the LPS of Y. regensburguei is characterized by the presence of a novel core oligosac-charide type, which is composed of an undeca-saccharide.
the Yokenella lipopolysacchrides are composed of an immunotype-dependent core oligosacchride, which differs only by the presence of a single hexose residue.
the structures of two immunologically non-related core oligosacchaides of Y. regensburgi LPS were elucidated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of two novel, nonrelated core oligo- saccharides of Y. regensburgi LPS, differing only by a terminal hexose residue.

the structural elucidation of two immunologically nonrelated core structures of the Y. regensburgei serotypes O:1 and O:2, which are distinguished by a single substitution of a terminal alpha-d-Gal residue for alpha-d-Glucose.
the identification of a novel core oligosac-charide type in Y. regensburguei LPS, which has not been described so far.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the core oligo- and polysaccharide of Y. regensburgae is not a typical one, and it is not a typical example of the LPS structure, which is a characteristic feature for the genus Yersinia.

the core oligo- and polysaccharides of LPS of the Y. regensburgei strains are novel structures, which are serologically non-related and differ only by the presence/absence of a single hexose residue in the outermost terminal position of the core oligo-/polysaccharides.
the LPS of Y. regensburgi is characterized by a novel core oligosac-charide type, which differs from the known core structures of the other gram-negative bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have characterized two novel immunotypes of Y. regensburgi LPS, differing only by the presence or absence of a single hexopyranosyl residue.

the LPS of Y. regensburguei strains can be classified as a novel immunological type of LPS, which differs from the other known immunological types of LPS only by a single substitution of a hexose residue.
we have described two novel core oligosaccha- rides of the Y. Regensburgei strain PCM 2474 and strain PCM 2475.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the core structure of the LPS of Y. regensburgae is a novel type of core structure, which is not present in the LPS of the related species Y. regensburghi and is not related to the LPS core of any other bacterial species.
the LPS core structure can be a powerful marker for the classification of bacterial species.
the structure of the core is a key factor in defining the antigenic properties of the bacterial cells.
